original_question: Consider the one-dimensional Fredrickson-Andersen one-spin facilitated model (FA-1f) on Z, where each site updates only when at least one nearest neighbor is infected, and where the reversible equilibrium measure pi is the Bernoulli product measure with infected density q in (0,1). For any such q and any local observable f depending on finitely many sites, does the law of the process started from any initial distribution nu that almost surely contains at least one infected site satisfy lim_{t->infinity} |E_nu[f(eta(t))] - pi(f)| = 0?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in Section 1.1 ("State of the art and some conjectures"): for FA-1 on Z, for any q in (0,1) and any function f depending on finitely many vertices, one asks whether lim_{t->infinity}|E_nu[f(eta(t))]-pi(f)|=0 provided nu(exists an infected vertex)=1. ([emergentmind.com](https://www.emergentmind.com/open-problems/fa-1f-convergence-from-infected-initial-state?utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's target: it has the correct one-dimensional FA-1/FA-1f setting on Z, the correct parameter range q in (0,1), the correct class of test functions (local/finitely supported observables), the correct initial-law hypothesis (almost surely at least one infected vertex), and the correct asymptotic claim (convergence of local expectations to pi). ([emergentmind.com](https://www.emergentmind.com/open-problems/fa-1f-convergence-from-infected-initial-state?utm_source=openai))
missing_details: Make explicit that the process lives on the configuration space {0,1}^Z and that nu is a probability measure on this space; the paper states the hypothesis as nu(exists an infected vertex)=1. ([emergentmind.com](https://www.emergentmind.com/open-problems/fa-1f-convergence-from-infected-initial-state?utm_source=openai))

Spell out the legal refresh dynamics so the question is fully stand-alone: a site may update only when at least one nearest neighbor is infected, and a legal update resamples that site to infected with probability q and healthy with probability 1-q.

Say explicitly that f:{0,1}^Z->R is a local function, i.e. it depends on finitely many coordinates; this is the paper's exact test class. ([emergentmind.com](https://www.emergentmind.com/open-problems/fa-1f-convergence-from-infected-initial-state?utm_source=openai))
Identify E_nu as expectation for the FA-1 process started from the initial law nu.

Avoid wording that suggests a stronger infinite-volume mode of convergence than the paper asks for: Conjecture 1.1 is formulated through convergence against every local function. ([emergentmind.com](https://www.emergentmind.com/open-problems/fa-1f-convergence-from-infected-initial-state?utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Let (eta_t)_{t>=0} be the one-dimensional Fredrickson-Andersen one-spin facilitated process (FA-1) on Z, with state space {0,1}^Z, in which a site x may refresh only if at least one of its nearest neighbors x-1 or x+1 is infected, and upon a legal refresh the site becomes infected with probability q and healthy with probability 1-q, independently of the past. Let pi be the Bernoulli product equilibrium measure with infected density q, where q in (0,1). Is it true that, for every initial probability measure nu on {0,1}^Z satisfying nu(there exists at least one infected vertex)=1, and for every local function f:{0,1}^Z->R depending on finitely many coordinates, one has lim_{t->infinity} |E_nu[f(eta_t)] - pi(f)| = 0?
justification: The draft is already essentially Conjecture 1.1, so the right refinement is to make the ambient state space, the legal refresh rule, and the meaning of local function/expectation explicit without broadening the scope. I therefore kept the exact quantifier structure and the minimal initial-data hypothesis from Conjecture 1.1, and I did not replace it by the neighboring stronger exponential-relaxation problem discussed separately in the same introductory context. The nearby introduction also emphasizes that current rigorous results only cover more restrictive regimes or assumptions, so the refined question should remain this narrow global local-equilibrium conjecture. ([emergentmind.com](https://www.emergentmind.com/open-problems/fa-1f-convergence-from-infected-initial-state?utm_source=openai))
